threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers: they still queue for the 106 bus instead of walking to the next stop like everyone else.
Last night on the 196, I watched a guy try to pay with an old £1 coin. The driver just shook his head but the next passenger handed him a donut instead.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home was when I heard a street musician playing accordion at 3 a.m. while people outside debated the best döner in town.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery. It’s a strange mix of grilled meat and abstract expressionism, but it works.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their reaction to the BART delays; non-locals panic, while we just pull out snacks and settle in for the wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 Fulton halted for a dog on the tracks yesterday. Drivers had to wait while a guy coaxed it with treats—only in SF!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for Instagram. But locals know they’re the heartbeats where impromptu concerts and chess games pop up.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily: they still stare in awe at the TNC trailers outside the metro, trying to decipher if it's a food truck or a film set.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still try to catch the Tube during rush hour, thinking it’ll save time. The packed platforms tell a different story.
Last night on the 68, a couple whispered their whole breakup saga. Must’ve been a quiet stop, because we all heard every word.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a guy in a full suit calmly ordering a kebab at 2 AM while a street musician played beside him. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM, then stumble into a late-night techno party hidden behind a kebab shop. It's a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the best burrito spot isn’t the one on every Instagram account, it’s the hole in the wall on 24th that closes at 3 PM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni stuck behind a guy walking a goat on Larkin. Only in San Francisco do you see someone casually taking their pet for a ride on the bus route.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume Gràcia is just a party zone. They miss the quiet mornings with locals sipping café amb llet and the kids biking to school.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their struggle with the metro ticket machines—staring at the screen like it's an alien spaceship.
